version.changelog:
- Initial release of office-toolkit, providing tools for reading, creating, and editing Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx/.csv), PowerPoint (.pptx), and PDF documents.
- Utilizes python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, and pypdf libraries for core functionality.
- Supports document conversion and additional features via pandoc and LibreOffice.
- Includes code examples and formatting guidelines for typical Office file operations.
- Specifies dependency installation steps and agent rules for robust document handling.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Office document helper, but its setup instructions ask users to modify the host system with privileged, unpinned installs.

dimensions.detail: The manifest reports no required binaries while the skill text relies on pandoc, LibreOffice, and pdftoppm-style PDF rendering, so the runtime footprint is under-declared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The setup block recommends pip install --break-system-packages and sudo apt install without pinning versions, hashes, virtual environment guidance, or explicit warning about host-level changes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Document file reads, writes, conversion with pandoc, and LibreOffice fallback are mostly purpose-aligned, though pandas, pdftoppm, and external tool use are broader than the core library list.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact declares no credentials and no persistence, and inspection found no background services, memory writes, credential access, exfiltration, or automatic execution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The instructions focus on reading, creating, and editing Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files, which matches the stated office-toolkit purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the setup commands before installing. Prefer a virtual environment, avoid --break-system-packages, only run sudo apt install if you trust your OS package sources, and keep backups when editing existing documents.
llm.findings:
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact explicitly documents unpinned system-wide Python and OS package installation, including --break-system-packages and sudo.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted for the install guidance: privileged and system-wide setup is not proportionately scoped or sufficiently warned for a documentation-style Office skill.
[PE2] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern rather than malicious: sudo is used for ordinary package installation, but it still grants high-impact host modification authority.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded: pandoc and LibreOffice are normal document-processing tools and are disclosed in the skill text, though they increase the processing attack surface.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded for file creation/editing examples: writing output Office/PDF files is central to the skill, but users should avoid overwriting originals without backups.
[SDI-1] expected: Partially accepted as under-disclosure: pandas and pdftoppm are adjacent to Office/PDF workflows, but they are not fully reflected in the metadata.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-only credential text is a quality/localization issue, not evidence of unsafe behavior.
